title: Product promo
summary: A launch film, promo or product ad of 15-60 s for a product or app: motion design built around the real product, its mechanism and one proposition.

notFor.when: the film teaches how to use the product step by step
an animated film with no product to sell: kinetic type, logo animation, music-driven motion
a story or mood film made from AI-generated shots, where generation is the point
a brand or event montage or sizzle reel cut to music from stock or supplied footage
a what's-new, release or feature-update video about something already shipped in an existing product
the preview video for an App Store or Google Play product page
a teaser or trailer before a launch or event that withholds the product, builds anticipation or announces a date
a creator, customer or UGC-style ad filmed on a phone by a person talking about the product

alternatives.when: the user supplies the footage, the script, the word timings and the proof, and wants it assembled into a hook-problem-demo-proof-CTA ad

qa: With sound off, frame 90 (3 s) already shows the product or its effect and the proposition can be read
Every claim on screen is shown happening in the real product within the same shot or the next one
The end card lands on a downbeat, holds at least 2 s without a fade and keeps the CTA out of the platform's bottom safe zone

intake.ask: Where can I see and capture the real product: URL, build, test account, device or files?
intake.why: Every product shot must be the real product (docs/real-ui.md); without it nothing can be built honestly.

intake.ask: Where will it run, and is it a paid ad or an organic post?
intake.why: Placement sets length, formats and safe zones (profiles); a paid Reels ad cannot use licensed music and a TikTok ad with AI media needs a disclaimer.
intake.default: A paid vertical 9:16 ad of 30 s for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, with a 15 s cut-down

intake.ask: What should the viewer do at the end, and where (URL, store, handle)?
intake.why: The end card carries one action and one place; three CTAs is an anti-pattern.
intake.default: Visit the product's site, shown as its URL

intake.ask: What does your viewer use today instead of the product?
intake.why: The strategist names the strongest alternative so the proposition fails when its name is swapped in.
intake.default: The strategist proposes it from the category; the user confirms at the strategy step

intake.ask: Which proof may the film show: a measured number, a named customer, a before and after?
intake.why: Claims on screen must be working claims in product-truth.json; numbers and customer names need a source and permission.
intake.default: Only product behaviour shown on screen; no numbers or customer names

profiles.note: In-feed ads run up to 60 s and 21-34 s performs best; hook in the first 3 s; text inside TikTok's safe-zone file; AI-generated or AI-altered media takes the mandatory disclaimer.
9:16; keep 14% top, 35% bottom and 6% each side free of text, logos and the CTA; no licensed music in Reels ads. Length band is a house rule (Meta allows up to 15 min).
Action ads 10-30 s, 9:16; only the first 60 s play in the feed; the CTA button appears from 3 s and the right rail holds the like and share buttons; music or voice raises conversions over 20%.
Skippable in-stream: the skip button appears at 5 s, so the product shows before it; Google advises under 3 min. The 60 s cap for a promo is a house rule.

15-30 s qualifies for every feed placement (in-stream to 90 s); under 30 s it loops, so the end card runs into the opening; SRT captions are text only; LinkedIn lists less than 30 fps: verify at upload.
Video ad cards take 16:9 and 1:1; promoted video may run to 10 min. The 6-30 s band is a house rule, a starting point.
A page hero autoplays muted (browsers allow sound only after a user gesture): the proposition must read without sound. 60 s is a house rule; Wistia engagement holds to about 5 min.

starter.note: Proof at reading scale, the product carrying the cut, a result as a change, a restrained close. paper-signal fits a light developer or data product; a dark SaaS starts from linear-midnight, a consumer app from pale-tint-app.

variants.title: AI ad
variants.changes: Add --secondary ai-video with an authorised --max-cost-usd. Generated shots carry the world, people or mood; the product's screens and object stay real (capture:app, asset:import). Key frames are approved before any video spend (skill model-and-asset-production). TikTok's AI-generated disclaimer is mandatory: the brief records the disclosure for every placement.

variants.title: B2B launch
variants.changes: LinkedIn profile first: square, 15-30 s for every feed placement or up to 90 s in-stream, built for sound off with burned captions and an SRT. Proofs are sourced numbers, named integrations and customer logos used with permission, each a working claim. The CTA is a demo or trial. A customer telling their own story is the case-study playbook.
